name: PRF (platelet-rich fibrin)
lead: Platelet-rich fibrin (PRF), also called leukocyte- and platelet-rich fibrin (L-PRF), is a derivative of platelet-rich plasma in which a person's own platelets and white blood cells are held in a fibrin matrix. Blood is drawn without anticoagulant and centrifuged immediately, producing a clot layer between platelet-poor plasma and red cells. [1] A 2006 series of papers by Dohan, Choukroun and colleagues described it as a 'second-generation platelet concentrate'. [2][3][4]

PRF is used mainly in oral and maxillofacial surgery for socket preservation, sinus lifts, periodontal regeneration and regenerative endodontics. [1] In looksmaxxing forums it is discussed as an under-eye treatment for dark circles and eye bags, and as a component of DIY or clinic-made facial serums. [5][6][7] Published trials are dental; none examined under-eye appearance.

paras: Wikipedia describes PRF as differing from PRP by retaining leukocytes and forming a fibrin scaffold, and states that activated platelets release growth factors such as PDGF, TGF-beta, VEGF and EGF. The article argues the fibrin matrix is central to its therapeutic potential. [1] A 2009 classification in Trends in Biotechnology sorted platelet concentrates into four categories by leukocyte and fibrin content, from pure PRP to leukocyte- and platelet-rich fibrin, noting that applications had been confusing because each method yields a different product. [8]

PRF is made from the person's own blood. Blood is drawn into tubes without anticoagulant and immediately spun in a tabletop centrifuge, typically for a few minutes at moderate speed, which separates it into platelet-poor plasma on top, a fibrin clot containing platelets and leukocytes in the middle, and red cells below; the clot is then lifted out and trimmed [1]. As the clot forms, activated platelets release growth factors including PDGF, TGF-beta, VEGF and EGF, and the fibrin network is argued to hold those signals in place longer than a liquid concentrate would [1].

Spin speed and tube type shape the product. A 2024 review in Periodontology 2000 explains that low-speed centrifugation, horizontal rather than fixed-angle rotors, chemically unmodified tubes and temperature control are all used to raise cell and growth-factor concentrations [17]. A 2016 laboratory comparison measured the release of growth factors from PRP, PRF and advanced PRF (A-PRF) [18].

The 2006 series by Dohan Ehrenfest, Choukroun and colleagues presented PRF as a second-generation platelet concentrate, with parts covering technology, platelet biology and clinical effects on tissue healing [2][3][4]. The 2009 classification by Dohan Ehrenfest and colleagues sorted platelet products into four families by leukocyte and fibrin content, from pure PRP to leukocyte- and platelet-rich fibrin (L-PRF) [8].

Until 2014 PRF was available only as a solid clot. Changes to centrifugation protocols and tube technology produced a liquid injectable form, i-PRF, and a 2024 review traces a decade of its use in periodontology, implantology, endodontics, temporomandibular-joint injections, orthodontic tooth movement, sports injuries and osteoarthritis, diabetic wounds, facial esthetics and hair regrowth [20]. Another group developed extended PRF (e-PRF or Alb-PRF), in which a brief heating step turns the albumin-rich plasma layer into an injectable gel with a resorption time of months rather than two to three weeks; the authors of that review list facial aesthetics among its applications [21]. In the US, PRF falls under FDA product code KST as a blood-draw hematology product that is exempt from 510(k) [1].

PRF is used mainly in oral and maxillofacial surgery. Wikipedia lists ridge preservation after extraction, sinus lifts before implants, periodontal regeneration, gingival recession as an alternative to connective-tissue grafts, guided bone regeneration and regenerative endodontics [1]. A 2023 narrative review reports PRF use after third-molar extractions, for alveolar osteitis and trismus, and in implant surgery [22].

On looksmax.org PRF comes up as an under-eye treatment, a clinic-delivered 'filler' and a base for do-it-yourself serums. One poster described a result as the best treatment for dark under-eye coloring and eyebags and relayed a doctor's view that PRF outperforms PRP [5]. A user preparing for a PRF filler session for dark circles invited updates, and a later reply in that thread reported no effect from the same treatment, saying that the mechanism would help in theory only when dark circles are age related [6]. A third poster described combining a commercial PRP base serum with a PRF tube drawn after a clinic facial to try to keep platelets, growth factors and fibrin in a personal serum, and noted that the commercial version of the idea was priced at hundreds of euros [7].
These are anecdotes. Wikipedia and the cited reviews describe PRF protocols that are carried out in clinical settings with defined centrifugation steps [1][17].

Human trials are mostly dental. A systematic review of 35 randomized trials through May 2016 found PRF had been investigated mainly in periodontology, for intrabony defects and gingival recession, where the majority of studies reported favorable soft-tissue results, with few randomized trials for extraction-socket management [23]. A 2025 meta-analysis of randomized trials of furcation defects compared PRF with open-flap debridement, bone graft, membranes and other regenerative materials [24]. Wikipedia cites a meta-analysis reporting better clinical and radiographic periodontal outcomes with PRF than open flap debridement alone, comparable to demineralized freeze-dried bone allograft [1]. A 2023 narrative review concluded that PRP and PRF in oral surgery show promising results but that protocols are inconsistent and further research is needed [22].

Recent randomized trials include ridge preservation with L-PRF [25] and with titanium-prepared PRF [26], low-speed PRF in intra-osseous defects of stage-III periodontitis [27], PRF with xenograft in sinus floor elevation [28], gingival perfusion during early socket healing in 62 patients [29], and L-PRF membranes versus a hemostatic agent at palatal donor sites in 42 patients [30]. Registered studies cover ridge preservation with L-PRF and A-PRF [9], PRF versus xenograft in closed sinus lift [10], shallow periodontal pockets [11], extraction sockets [12], lower third-molar surgery and facial swelling [13], regenerative endodontics in immature teeth [14], and thickening thin gingival phenotype with injectable PRF [15][16]. Their sample sizes range from 10 to 60 participants.
No study of PRF for dark circles, under-eye bags or other cosmetic outcomes was found.

lore.intro: On looksmax.org, PRF is discussed for dark under-eye circles and in homemade serums, with mixed personal reports. [5][6][7]

claims.claim: PRF is a strong treatment for dark under-eye colour and eye bags
claims.believers: A thread titled as a PRF result calls it the best treatment for dark under-eye coloring and eyebags, with the poster relaying a doctor's view that PRF outperforms PRP. [5]
claims.experts: No published study of PRF for under-eye appearance was identified; published PRF trials concern dental and oral surgery. [1][9]

claims.claim: PRF filler for dark circles did not work for some users
claims.believers: In one thread, a user who had the treatment reported no effect and said its mechanism would only help in theory if the dark circles were age related. [6]
claims.experts: No controlled data exist for this use. [1]

claims.claim: PRP or PRF serums can be made at home from one's own blood
claims.believers: A poster described making a personalised serum from a PRP base and a PRF tube after a clinic facial, to try to keep platelets, growth factors and fibrin in the product. [7]
claims.experts: Wikipedia notes PRF preparation relies on specific centrifugation without anticoagulant, and its clinical literature concerns clinic-prepared dental use; no studies of homemade facial serums were found. [1]

card.summary: Fibrin-clot cousin of PRP used in dental surgery and tried by forum users for under-eye circles; no facial trials found.
card.note: Published trials are dental; forum reports on dark circles are mixed.

quick.overview:
PRF is made by spinning a person's own blood without anticoagulant so that platelets and white cells are trapped in a fibrin clot. It is mainly a dental and oral surgery material for healing.
On looksmax.org some users try it for dark under-eye circles, with mixed reports and no published trials for that purpose.
quick.mechanism: Activated platelets in the fibrin matrix release growth factors such as PDGF, TGF-beta, VEGF and EGF, which is thought to support tissue healing.
quick.risks: Wikipedia does not discuss risks. Under-eye injection and homemade serums have no controlled safety data. PRF preparation falls under an FDA product code that is 510(k) exempt.

chain: Own blood is centrifuged into a fibrin clot or liquid rich in platelets
Growth factors released at the treated site in the skin
angle.text: In appearance circles PRF is used or discussed as an autologous injectable or serum ingredient for dark under-eye circles, eye bags and skin quality. Published trials focus on dental healing; user reports on forums are mixed.
